messages:
Jun: quick design question — for internal RPCs do we lean fully gRPC+proto and expose a translated JSON surface at the gateway, or do we offer first-class REST endpoints alongside gRPC? thinking about quotas, telemetry tags, and rollout UX.
Priya: +1 for proto-as-source-of-truth. generate http bindings with grpc-gateway, keep one canonical contract. less duplication that way.
Marco: cautious — grpc-gateway is fine for simple unary calls but streaming and bidi are awkward to translate. also we lose strong typing for enums/oneofs in some clients.
Diego: real ops concern: if we translate at the gateway we need consistent telemetry keys so we can attribute costs & latency back to the proto route (not just the generated path). otherwise billing/SLI dashboards get messy.
Alice: on quotas — do we enforce per-client-per-route tokens or per-request? for embeddings and generate we bill per-token, but a generic REST endpoint hides that nuance. customers hit quotas that don't map to cost.
Jun: what if gateway emits headers like `X-Proto-Service` and `X-Routing-Policy` so downstream systems (quota, billing, observability) can join on the proto identity?
Priya: that seems reasonable. gateway -> internal gRPC call adds headers: `X-Proto: models.Inference.Generate` and `X-Tokens-Estimate: 250` (when available).
Marco: would prefer a typed envelope in the internal RPC metadata rather than string headers — less brittle. e.g. metadata key `redwood-proto-id: models.Inference.Generate` and `redwood-routing: low-latency`. grpc metadata is straightforward.
Diego: agree on metadata. but gateway needs to calculate token estimates reliably — we should fail safe (omit estimate if unknown) and ensure quota system defaults to conservative limits.
Alice: and we should expose both quotas: a token quota (billing) and a request quota (abuse protection). different counters and UIs.
Jun: rollout UX — if we change the contract (proto change) how do we push to customers? canary at the gateway layer makes sense: route 1% traffic to new proto shape + mismatch logs.
Priya: +1 for canary with strict mismatch logs and a fallback to old shape. also versioned proto packages help: `models.v1.Inference` -> `models.v2.Inference`.
Marco: implementation nit: prefer an adapter pattern in the gateway: a small shim per service that translates incoming JSON to the canonical proto. avoids huge monolithic proto-translator codepath.
Diego: ops checklist for that shim: emit `redwood-proto-id`, `redwood-routing-policy`, and `redwood-canary-variant` metadata; produce structured telemetry entries with these tags; log mismatches at debug.
Alice: UI ask: in Console we need separate dashboards per quota type (tokens vs requests), plus a routing policy breakdown (percentage routed to low-latency vs cost-optimized). can we get telemetry keys aligned to those?
Jun: action items: Priya to draft proto header metadata RFC; Marco to prototype per-service shim pattern; Diego to update quota service to accept proto-id + optional token-estimate; Alice to sketch Console widgets for token vs request quotas. I'll coordinate the canary rollout plan.
infra-bot: noted — created ticket INF-2143: "proto-metadata-and-gateway-shim" and assigned to Priya/Marco/Diego/Alice. :white_check_mark:
Priya: quick code example of what I'm proposing for HTTP binding (grpc proto):
```proto
service Inference {
  rpc Generate(GenerateRequest) returns (GenerateResponse) {
    option (google.api.http) = {
      post: "/v1/inference:generate"
      body: "*"
    };
  }
}
```
Jun: example of header propagation we want (gateway -> internal):
```
redwood-proto-id: models.v2.Inference.Generate
redwood-routing-policy: low-latency
redwood-canary-variant: v2-shim
redwood-tokens-estimate: 320
```
Marco: minor point — ensure auth/impersonation headers are preserved when translating. gateway should assert auth and then inject `x-internal-auth: <signed>` for internal calls.
Diego: noted. also add a telemetry tag `gateway:grpc-gw` vs `gateway:raw-proxy` so we can split perf baselines.
Alice: UI mockups incoming, will attach to the ticket.
Jun: ok — let's keep the public surface stable (HTTP JSON bindings) but treat proto as the contract and use a small, testable shim in the gateway to translate and emit metadata. we track tokens + requests separately in Console and use canaries for proto changes.
Priya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
